hero.headline: We started this to do things differently.
hero.subtext: We've lived the challenges of growing a business with disconnected systems, limited resources, and solutions that didn't quite fit. We've also worked with consultants who brought rigid frameworks, pushed software, and overlooked how the business actually runs day to day. That's not how we work. We partner with businesses to build practical, flexible systems that support how they actually operate; without unnecessary complexity, cost, or rigid frameworks. We believe the best work happens through real partnership; which is why we choose to work with clients who value collaboration, transparency, and doing things the right way.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.text: To make operations easy; not in a naive way, but in the way that comes from having the right systems, the right data, and the right processes working together. We give growing teams the connected infrastructure they need to grow without the chaos, without bloated consulting fees, and without cookie-cutter solutions that don't fit.

faq.q: Are the tools really free?
faq.a: Yes. There is no sign-up and no paywall. Your inputs stay in your browser and nothing is stored.

faq.q: Where does the data come from?
faq.a: Each tool names its sources on the page: Statistics Canada, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics and the Australian Bureau of Statistics for wages, and the official code lists from Public Services and Procurement Canada, the U.S. General Services Administration and the European Union for codes.

faq.q: Will a tool tell me what Awesoon charges?
faq.a: No. Each result is about your own work, like your own labour cost. Pricing only comes after a call about your scope.

meta.title: Manual work cost calculator: what repeat admin work costs you
meta.description: Free calculator that turns hours of manual data entry, order and billing work into a yearly labour cost, using official wage data for Canadian provinces, U.S. states and Australian states.

calc.title: What does manual work cost your team each year?
calc.text: Pick your region and the roles doing repeat work. The wages come from public data for your region, so the number is yours. No sign-up.
calc.ukSoon: UK wage data coming soon. We will add regional earnings from the Office for National Statistics as soon as we can read it reliably.
calc.privacy: Your inputs stay in your browser.
calc.perYear: a year in wages spent on manual work
calc.pickRole: Pick at least one role to see your cost.
calc.basis: 52 weeks a year, wages only. Benefits, payroll taxes and overhead come on top, so your real cost is higher. Hours are split evenly across the roles you picked. This is your own labour cost, not an Awesoon price.
calc.usNote: Median annual wage for each occupation (SOC {codes}), turned into an hourly rate at 2,080 hours a year, the way BLS does.
calc.caNote: Median hourly wage for {occupation} ({code}). Statistics Canada does not publish these four roles separately, so the same broad figure is used for each role.
calc.auNote: {occupation}. This is not role specific and includes part-time staff, so it is a rough guide; it is turned into an hourly rate at 38 hours a week, the full-time week in the National Employment Standards.
calc.summary: {region}: {hours} hours a week, {people} people, about {cost} a year in wages.

faq.q: How is the cost worked out?
faq.a: Hours per week times people times 52 weeks gives your yearly hours. Each role's share of those hours is multiplied by the published wage for your region. Nothing is added for benefits or overhead, so the real figure is higher.

faq.q: Why is the Canadian wage the same for every role?
faq.a: Statistics Canada publishes wages for the broad group these roles belong to, administrative and financial support occupations, not for each clerk role. We show that figure rather than guess.

faq.q: Why is the UK not available?
faq.a: The regional earnings tables from the Office for National Statistics could not be read reliably when this snapshot was taken. UK regions will appear once they can.

faq.q: Is this what automation would save?
faq.a: No. It is what the manual work costs today. How much of it can be removed depends on your systems, and that is what a discovery call works out.

finder.text: Type a service. Get its UNSPSC, GSIN, PSC and CPV codes, with a plain note on where each one is used. No sign-up.

UNSPSC.name: UNSPSC
UNSPSC.explain: The United Nations Standard Products and Services Code. Canadian federal buyers and many others tag tenders with it.

GSIN.name: GSIN
GSIN.explain: Goods and Services Identification Number. Older Canadian federal notices still use it, so it is worth listing.

PSC.name: PSC
PSC.explain: Product and Service Code. U.S. federal contracts record what was bought with it.

CPV.name: CPV
CPV.explain: Common Procurement Vocabulary. EU and UK public notices are classified with it.

sources.UNSPSC: UNSPSC and GSIN copy and the GSIN to UNSPSC crosswalk: contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada (Public Services and Procurement Canada).
sources.PSC: PSC: Product and Service Codes from the U.S. General Services Administration, served by USAspending.gov. U.S. Government work, public domain.
sources.CPV: CPV: Publications Office of the European Union, Common Procurement Vocabulary, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Reused with attribution; the EU does not endorse this tool.

faq.q: Which code should I use?
faq.a: Use the scheme the buyer uses. Canadian federal tenders use UNSPSC and sometimes GSIN, U.S. federal contracts use PSC and NAICS, and EU and UK notices use CPV. Listing several close codes helps buyers find you.

faq.q: Are these codes official?
faq.a: Yes. They come from the official lists published by Public Services and Procurement Canada, the U.S. General Services Administration and the Publications Office of the European Union. Always check the code in the official list before you bid.

faq.q: Why can I not find NAICS?
faq.a: NAICS is not loaded into this finder yet. It will be added once the list is in.

faq.q: Why only IT, design and advertising codes?
faq.a: This finder is built for the services Awesoon works in, which keeps it small and fast. Other families may come later.

gamesPrivacy.title: Privacy policy, Awesoon games
gamesPrivacy.updated: Last updated 10 November 2026. Version 2, for game versions 1.1.0 and later. Earlier versions show no ads and collect nothing.
gamesPrivacy.lead: Our games run on your device. The only data that leaves it is what the advertising software collects, and you make the choices.
gamesPrivacy.appliesTo: Applies to all ten Awesoon games: Stack Snap, Loop Weaver, Tidy Tiles, Penny Loaf, Quick Trivia Blitz, Dodge Rush, Word Chain Dash, Color Match Frenzy, Knot Untangle and Bounce Blitz. The games are published by Awesoon Technologies Inc., a company in British Columbia, Canada.

p: There is no account, no sign-in and no server of ours. Your progress, scores, statistics, settings and the answer to the age question are stored on the device itself. They are never sent to us or to anyone else. The games collect nothing, and this website uses analytics only with your consent.

The first time you open a game, it asks your birth month and year. Nothing is filled in beforehand. The answer stays on your device, is never sent to us or to Google, and cannot be changed by going back. It decides which ads you see. On iPhone and iPad, if Apple tells the game your device belongs to someone under 13, that overrides your answer. On Android, the game follows your answer alone.

sections.h: Advertising and what Google AdMob collects
p: The games show ads served by Google AdMob. Its software is built into each game. It may collect your advertising ID, your IP address and device data such as the device model, system version, language and how you interact with ads. Google uses this to show and measure ads and to prevent fraud. The data goes to Google, under Google's own privacy policy at policies.google.com/privacy. We do not receive it. We see only aggregate earnings reports.

sections.h: Your choices if you are 13 or over
p: On iPhone and iPad, the game asks for your permission to track you. If you decline, you still see ads, but they are not personalised. In the European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland, Google's consent form runs before any personalised ads, and a row in the game's Settings reopens it so you can change your answer. On Android you can reset or delete your advertising ID in your device's settings.

sections.h: Penny Loaf: which ads it shows
p: Penny Loaf shows rewarded ads that you choose to watch for a bonus, such as a ten minute rush, doubled away earnings, a free look at a rival or a district opening sooner. A reward you earn is always given. One full-screen ad may show after a buyout scene closes, never during a celebration and not in the first sessions after install. It shows no banner ads and no ads when the app opens. In Settings, the Ad choices row reopens Google's consent form.

Our games are for players of all ages. We ask your birth month and year once, on your device only. If you are under 13, ads are limited to a child-safe setting and no advertising ID is used. Players under 13 still play the whole game. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. A parent or guardian who has a question can write to us at the address below.

Progress and settings stay on your device until you delete the game or reset it. Emails you send us are deleted 12 months after our last reply. Ad data is held by Google under its own policies. We hold none of it. Several games also have a reset option in Settings that clears progress without deleting the app.

We hold almost nothing about players: only the emails you send us. If you live in the European Economic Area or the UK (GDPR and UK GDPR), in Brazil (LGPD) or in California (CCPA and CPRA), you can ask us for a copy of what we hold about you, ask us to correct or delete it, object to or restrict how it is used, and withdraw consent you gave. In the EEA, the UK and Brazil you can also complain to your data protection authority. Where we rely on consent, which is the case for personalised ads, you can withdraw it at any time using the choices above.

We do not sell personal information. Ad data that Google collects through its software can count as sharing for advertising under California law. If you are 13 or over you can opt out by declining the tracking prompt or the consent form, and under 13 no advertising ID is used. We do not treat you differently for using these rights. Write to us to use any of them. We reply within the time your local law sets: one month under GDPR and UK GDPR, 15 days under Brazilian law and 45 days under California law. Requests about ad data held by Google go to Google as well.
If this policy changes, the new version is posted on this page with a new date above, before the game version that needs it is released. Earlier versions stay posted, and version 1 is linked below.

gamesPrivacyV1.intro: Each game runs entirely on your device. There is no account, no sign-in and no server. Your progress, scores, statistics and settings are stored on the device itself, and they are never sent to us or to anyone else.

p: Nothing. We do not collect your name, email address, contacts, location, photos, device identifiers or usage analytics. Nothing you do in a game leaves your phone.

The current versions of these games show no advertising. If a future version does, this page is updated before that version is released, and the update names the advertising provider and what it collects.
Because everything is stored on your device, deleting a game deletes all of it. Several of the games also have a reset option in Settings that clears progress without deleting the app.
These games are not directed at children under 13, and because they collect nothing, they hold no data about anyone of any age.
If this policy changes, the new version is posted on this page with a new date above.

platforms.title: The platforms we actually know
platforms.text: We are vendor-neutral. We pick what fits your operations, not what pays a commission.

fit.netsuite: Cloud-first ERP for multi-entity businesses with strong finance and reporting needs. A strong pick for companies that outgrew QuickBooks.
fit.odoo: All-in-one suite: ERP, CRM, inventory, ecommerce. Ideal when you want one connected stack without per-module lock-in.
fit.epicor: Deep manufacturing and distribution ERP with complex production workflows, BOMs and shop floor control.
fit.sap: SAP-grade financial controls and audit trails without the overhead of a full S/4HANA deployment.
fit.salesforce: Sales-led teams with complex pipelines, custom objects and high forecast accuracy needs.
fit.hubspot: Marketing-driven teams that want fast adoption, inbound workflows and tight sales and marketing alignment.
fit.zoho: A full CRM suite without enterprise pricing. Good for lean teams that need breadth without complexity.
fit.pipedrive: Simple pipeline visibility for small sales teams that want speed over configuration depth.
fit.shopify: Our default for B2C and mid-complexity B2B. Fast to launch, easy to run, huge app ecosystem.
fit.magento: Complex catalogs, tiered B2B pricing and deep customization, for when Shopify is not enough.
fit.woocommerce: Content-driven stores on WordPress with full ownership of hosting and plugins.
fit.bigcommerce: Hybrid SaaS and headless, with stronger native B2B features than Shopify Basic.
fit.celigo: Integration platform built for NetSuite and ecommerce, with connectors for the stack we see most.
fit.boomi: Enterprise integration with strong data transformation, governance and error handling.
fit.zapier: Fast app-to-app automation when speed matters more than depth. Good for non-critical workflows.
fit.make: Visual workflow builder with deeper logic than Zapier, for complex multi-step flows.
fit.openai: GPT-based copilots, reasoning and document intelligence.
fit.anthropic: Claude for long-context analysis, production agents and safer tool use.
fit.langchain: Framework for building RAG pipelines, agents and multi-step AI workflows.
fit.postgresql: Our default database, with pgvector for AI embeddings and no separate vector store.

faq.q: What is business automation?
faq.a: It is having your systems pass data and tasks to each other, so people stop re-typing and chasing. A person still approves anything that needs judgment.

faq.q: Which systems can you connect?
faq.a: Most business tools with an API or export, such as Shopify, NetSuite, QuickBooks, HubSpot and Salesforce. We tell you on the discovery call if something cannot be connected cleanly.

faq.q: What happens when a connection fails?
faq.a: Every flow we build logs its work and alerts a named person when something fails, with a written fix-it guide.

faq.q: Do we own the automations?
faq.a: Yes. They run in accounts you own and are documented so your team or another provider can take over.

software-development.name: Software development
software-development.metaDescription: Custom software development for businesses: apps, APIs, databases and interfaces built around how your team works, with the code in your name.
software-development.title: Software development: custom tools for the work products cannot do.
software-development.answer: Custom software development builds the apps, APIs, databases and screens your business needs when no product on the market fits. Awesoon builds them in small steps you can see, and you own the code, the accounts and the documentation.

choose.label: We need a tool no product offers
Our app slows down or breaks under load
Partners need to connect to our data
Our screens are hard to use

faq.q: Should we build custom software or buy a product?
faq.a: Buy when a product already does the job well. Build only when nothing fits, and we will say so if a product would do.

faq.q: Who owns the code?
faq.a: You do. It lives in your own repository from the first day, with hosting accounts in your name.

faq.q: How do you keep a build on track?
faq.a: We agree a short written scope, build in small steps you review, and change course early when something does not fit.

faq.q: Can you take over an existing app?
faq.a: Yes. We start with a written review of the code and tell you what we find before suggesting changes.

software-development.closingTitle: Describe the tool you wish you had.
software-development.closingText: A 30-minute discovery call with Ray, then a plain answer on whether to build, buy or connect. No obligation.

erp-crm.metaDescription: ERP and CRM implementation, setup and custom programming for growing businesses. Vendor neutral, no commissions, owner-led by Ray Rasouli.
erp-crm.title: ERP and CRM: systems that match how you actually work.
erp-crm.answer: ERP and CRM services choose, set up and extend the systems that run your orders, inventory, finance and sales. Awesoon is vendor neutral and takes no commissions, so the system fits your operations instead of the other way around.

choose.label: We are moving to a new ERP

We bought a CRM and nobody uses it

faq.q: Which ERP or CRM should we choose?
faq.a: It depends on your size, processes and other systems. Because we take no commissions, we compare options on fit alone.

faq.q: Why do ERP projects fail?
faq.a: Most fail on process and data, not software: unclear requirements, messy data and no owner. We start there.

faq.q: Do you support the system after go-live?
faq.a: Yes. Our ERP support and CRM support pages cover ongoing help after launch.

faq.q: Can you fix a system someone else set up?
faq.a: Yes. We review what is there, write down what we find and fix the parts that matter most first.

erp-crm.closingTitle: Get the system to fit the business.

We grew and our tools did not

faq.a: We review your systems and processes, compare options, and give you a written plan. You can act on it with us or anyone else.

faq.q: Are you tied to any software vendor?
faq.a: No. We take no commissions or referral fees, so our advice is about fit.

faq.q: What is the free systems health check?
